judgments.evidence: Broad low crown, visible outward scaffold, more connected lobes and selective warm surfaces are closer to references than the legacy pointed crown. Inner shoots modestly improve central coverage.
judgments.remaining: Still regular/flat in places; some center gaps/ring-like physical shadow remain. Generic broadleaf texture is not a dedicated acacia compound-leaf asset.

judgments.betterThanPrevious: Structurally distinct and more open; overall attractiveness is inconclusive
judgments.evidence: Five wind-biased scaffold paths, lean and larger exposed windows produce a different branch silhouette and visible support.
judgments.remaining: Crown is too fragmented into a few pads for the supplied mature umbrella target; not proven preferable to A.

judgments.evidence: Two leaders and staggered crown levels are structurally distinct, but foliage still reads as floating separate tiers.
judgments.remaining: Do not reject all layered crowns; this particular support/mass distribution needs a different implementation.

landscape: Warmer gold/straw and half added relief produce more expansive plains with distant geology preserved. Inner terrain and tree base coordinates remain unchanged.
grass: Cheaper true curved/cupped blades and sparse seed heads add local depth, but small separated midground marks remain; connected swaths/noise target is only partial.
robustness: A tested at29/41/73; no new exposed terrain edges in tested views. Wind/phase/specimen seeds vary morphology. B/C only seed29 controlled studies.
technicalVsArtistic: C has lower alpha-layer proxy than A but worse visual coherence. Deterministic attachment and lower triangle count do not approve art.
checkpointQuestion: Which tree direction should we develop next: A mature umbrella, B exposed wind-shaped, C layered, or reject all three?
